page: Amazon Web Services r8i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor offering 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at up to 3.9 GHz, paired with 480 MB of L3 cache. Direct hardware access is enabled with hypervisor absence and VMX virtualization flags active. The server delivers 1536.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 system memory at 7 GHz, preserving an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware lacks bundled local storage and includes 0 GPUs, while baseline network throughput is rated at 75 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core computational throughput and memory handling. The platform reaches a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 209,058.58 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,107.0, supported by extensive instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8. Memory throughput shows extreme parallel efficiency, recording 585.17 GB/sec for uncached read-only blocks and 296.12 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Extended instruction benchmarks and cryptographic performance also score in the upper decile.

The primary operational tradeoff centers on storage architecture. With no bundled local NVMe storage, disk throughput and persistence depend fully on external network-attached volumes over the 75 Gbps network interface. Single-core execution falls into the middle tiers, represented by a stress-ng single-core score of 2,143.9, meaning the platform derives its efficiency strictly from high-density multi-threaded parallelization rather than individual thread speeds.

Resource allocation and AMX matrix acceleration make the r8i.metal-48xl well positioned for massive in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, large-scale clang build farms, and CPU-based LLM inference. Its vast memory envelope and strong multi-threaded decompression rates of 1241.45 GB/sec also fit real-time analytical processing, multi-tenant container orchestration, and large-scale data transformation workflows.
